newsitem.title: UK: Royal mistress Camilla escapes car crash charges.
newsitem.headline: Royal mistress Camilla escapes car crash charges.

text.p: Camilla Parker Bowles, mistress to Britain's Prince Charles, will not be prosecuted over a car crash last month which left both drivers with minor injuries, police said on Friday.

Parker Bowles, 49, whose earthy style marks a stark contrast to Charles's ex-wife Diana, hurt her head and wrist in a head-on collision as she drove through twisting country lanes on her way to dinner at Charles's Highgrove home in Wiltshire, west England.
A spokeswoman for Wiltshire Police told Reuters they did not have sufficient evidence to bring charges against either driver.

Parker Bowles and 53-year-old interior designer Carolyn Melville-Smith passed alcohol tests at the time of the accident, which occurred on the evening of June 12 between the villages of Norton and Easton Grey.
Parker Bowles had telephoned police and ambulance services from her Ford Mondeo estate car.

Parker Bowles, who divorced cavalry officer Andrew Parker Bowles last year, owns a house about 20 miles (32 km) from the 48-year-old prince. She is a frequent guest at Highgrove, where she stables her horses.
Tall with wiry blond hair, she has graced television screens and the front pages of tabloid newspapers recently, as speculation mounts she may one day marry Charles, heir to the British throne.
Although their love affair has lasted some 20 years, some sections of the British public have been unwilling to accept Parker Bowles, portrayed as the woman who broke up the fairytale royal marriage.
Charles was divorced from Princess Diana, 36, in February 1996 and has ruled out remarrying.
